evidence.summary: The petitioners, representing rural agrarian villagers and vulnerable victims, seek immediate interim relief against the factory of Apex Dyechem Industries Ltd. and other respondents for the illegal discharge of toxic industrial effluent, causing severe chemical poisoning and endangering the lives of 42 victims, including pregnant women and infants. This case raises constitutional questions under Article 21 (right to life) and Article 14 (equality before law).

The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) has certified a forensic toxicology report on wastewater from Apex Dyechem Industries, finding it exceeds legal safety thresholds for heavy metals and COD. The Chief Scientific Officer, Dr. K. Radhokrishnan, recommends immediate total industrial shutdown due to the acute toxicological hazard. The case involves a dispute over industrial pollution and seeks relief under constitutional articles 21 and 14.

The Sub-Divisional Magistrate conducted a midnight raid on Apex Dyechem Industries Ltd. due to reports of mass poisoning in Chhatarpur village. The factory was found to be illegally bypassing its effluent treatment plant, pumping toxic wastewater into a rural stormwater channel. The operations manager was apprehended. The factory was sealed, and the main locks were sealed with lead seals. The case involves serious injury and the right to live with dignity (Article 21).
